place: Council Chambers, Municipal Hall, 37955 Second Avenue
preview: The main item is Mayor Easton's motion asking staff to redraw the 2027 budget with no increase in property tax revenue over 2026, along with a staff memo on how long that would take and what it would cost. Council will also give final approval to a rezoning on Westway Avenue and a business licence update for co-living, and consider changes to District fees.

agenda_items.plain: Council will decide whether to ask staff to bring back a new draft 2027 budget with no increase in property tax revenue over 2026, without layoffs and without cutting resident services.
agenda_items.ask: Should the District ask staff to redraw the 2027 budget so property tax revenue does not go up from 2026?
agenda_items.yes_means: Staff would prepare a revised draft 2027 budget with no property tax revenue increase, based on a review of how the District is organized and run.
agenda_items.no_means: Budget work would continue on the current draft 2027 to 2036 Financial Plan without this direction.
agenda_items.context: Mayor Easton gave notice of this motion at the November 17 meeting. It asks staff to rework the draft 2027 budget, part of the 2027 to 2036 Financial Plan (the District's 10 year spending plan), so the District collects no more property tax than in 2026. At council's request, staff have written a memo on the timing, costs and options, including smaller or phased approaches, and the effect on the schedule for adopting the Financial Plan.
facts: Target: no increase in municipal property tax revenue over 2026
Services residents use must stay the same or improve compared with 2026
No involuntary layoffs or cuts to regular hours of unionized staff
No extra contracting out to replace work done by unionized staff
Savings would come from a review led by the Chief Administrative Officer (the District's top staff member)
supporters: The motion aims to hold property taxes steady for residents in 2027
It looks for savings in management layers, overhead, duplicated work and approval processes
It protects jobs and services while seeking efficiencies
It asks for a clear report on effects on staffing, reserves, capital projects, debt and fees
concerns: Staff were asked to report how long the review would take and what work would be put on hold
The work could affect the timeline for adopting the 2027 to 2036 Financial Plan
There may be effects on planned or ongoing capital projects and purchasing
Savings may affect reserves, capital projects, debt or fees and charges
factors: Quality and timeliness of District services
Effects on roads, facilities and other capital projects
Use of savings, reserves and debt
agenda_items.for_you: If passed and followed through, the District's share of property taxes would not raise more money in 2027 than in 2026.

agenda_items.plain: Council will vote on first, second and third reading of changes to the District's Fees and Charges Bylaw, which sets what the District charges for services.
agenda_items.ask: Should the District approve the proposed changes to its fees and charges?
agenda_items.yes_means: The fee changes move forward and would need one more vote for final adoption.
agenda_items.no_means: Current District fees stay as they are for now.

agenda_items.plain: Council will vote on final adoption of a rezoning (changing what can be built on a piece of land) for 38320 Westway Avenue.
agenda_items.ask: Should the District give final approval to the rezoning of 38320 Westway Avenue?
agenda_items.yes_means: The new zoning for 38320 Westway Avenue takes effect.
agenda_items.no_means: The property keeps its current zoning.
agenda_items.for_you: Affects the property at 38320 Westway Avenue and its neighbours.

agenda_items.plain: Council will vote on final adoption of an update to the Business Licence Bylaw dealing with co-living (homes where several people rent rooms and share common spaces).
agenda_items.ask: Should the District adopt the business licence update for co-living housing?
agenda_items.yes_means: The updated business licence rules for co-living take effect.
agenda_items.no_means: The current business licence rules stay in place.

agenda_items.plain: Councillor Prosko proposes giving $250 from the 2026 council contingency fund as a donation for a holiday tree at the Squamish Adventure Centre.
agenda_items.ask: Should council give $250 from its contingency fund for a holiday tree at the Squamish Adventure Centre?
agenda_items.yes_means: The District donates $250 toward a holiday tree at the Adventure Centre.
agenda_items.no_means: No District money goes to the holiday tree.
agenda_items.for_you: A $250 donation from council's contingency fund.

agenda_items.plain: Council will hear a presentation and vote to formally recognize November 25 to December 10, 2026, as the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence.
Staff are sharing a memo for information on the Urban Forest Management Strategy, the District's plan for trees in town.
